name: John Fish
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: John Fish is the CEO and sole owner of the $7.4 billion (2025 revenues) Suffolk Construction, New England's largest general contractor.
Fish founded Suffolk in 1982 after his father seeded him $80,000 to start a non-union contractor in Boston.
Fish expanded Suffolk's U.S. footprint through the 1990s and 2000s, constructing buildings in the commercial, healthcare, higher-ed, K-12, airport, life sciences and gaming sectors.
Since 2019 Suffolk has invested over $75 million across more than 50 construction tech startups, including robotics and AI ventures.
Today Suffolk has 3500 employees. It has built over 200 million square feet of commercial real estate in the U.S. over the last 20 years.

name: John Dorrance III
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: John Dorrance is an heir to the Campbell's Soup fortune; his grandfather invented the Campbell's formula for condensed soup.
His relatives are still the company's largest shareholders, but he sold his stake in the mid-1990's and emigrated to Ireland.
His move was presumably timed to avoid capital gains taxes when he sold his Campbell's stake.
The Irish government reportedly gave Dorrance citizenship in 1995 when he spent $1.5 million planting trees.

name: Ka Yan Hui
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021-2024); Forbes annual (2010-2023); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Hui Ka Yan is chairman of Hong Kong-listed Evergrande Group, one of China's biggest real estate developers.
Evergrande, which Hui took public in 2009, has over 800 projects in more than 280 cities.
Hui worked as a technician in a steel factory for 10 years after graduating college in 1982.
Hui started Evergrande in Guangzhou in 1996 and began picking up low price properties in small markets. Its first project was Jinbi Garden.
Hui's son Xu Zhijian, who holds an MBA from prestigious Tsinghua University, is a vice president at Evergrande.
forbes_facts: Evergrande owns the majority of Guangzhou Evergrande, one of China's most successful soccer teams.

name: Koo Bon-neung
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1997-2024); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Koo Bon-neung runs Heesung Electronics, which makes display components for TVs, computers, tablets and smartphones.
He is the younger brother of Koo Bon-moo, the late chairman of the LG Group, one of the top five conglomerates in South Korea.
In 2004 his son Koo Kwang-mo was adopted by his brother, who lost his own son in a car accident. Kwang-mo now helms LG as its chairman.
forbes_facts: Koo is a former president of the Korea Baseball Organization.
He started his career in LG in 1976 as a manager for the company's branch in Chicago.

name: Brett Hildebrand
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Brett Hildebrand is a major shareholder of Credit One Bank, one of the largest subprime lenders in the United States.
Despite a nearly identical name and logo to the better known Capital One Bank, Credit One is entirely separate and caters mainly to low-credit borrowers.
After beginning his career at Goldman Sachs and Citigroup, Hildebrand cofounded Sherman Financial Group in 1998 with Ben Navarro, Credit One's controlling shareholder.
Sherman Financial built Resurgent Capital Services into one of America's largest debt collection businesses before selling the company in 2021.
Hildebrand has plowed his cash proceeds from Credit One into biotech, AI and fintech bets through his investment firm IAG Capital Partners.

name: Douglas Hsu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1998-2025)
forbes_bio: Douglas Hsu is chairman of Far Eastern Group, a conglomerate that his father started in mainland China in 1940 as an underwear supplier.
The company moved to Taiwan in 1949 after the civil war.
Far Eastern's businesses include Far EasTone Telecommunications, U-Ming Marine Transport, Everest Textile, Asia Cement and Oriental Union Chemical.
Hsu is a trustee emeritus at the University of Notre Dame, where he earned two degrees.

name: Luo Liguo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026)
forbes_bio: Luo Liguo is the chairman of Hoshine Silicon Industry, a supplier of silicon metals used in electronics, photovoltaic, and chemical products.
Hoshine went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2017.
Luo hails from a township famous for making straw hats. He started a successful straw hat business early in his career.
Luo's daughter, Luo Yi, is Hoshine's vice chairman. Her husband, Hao Han, is a company director.
Luo's son, Luo Yedong, has been Hoshine's CEO since 2021.

name: Qi Jinxing
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026)
forbes_bio: Qi Jinxing is the chairman of Hangzhou Binjiang Real Estate Group, a real estate developer headquartered in Hangzhou.
Qi got his first job in a government district office before moving on to a management position at a construction firm.
In 1996 he turned down a bigger government position to set up Hangzhou Binjiang.

name: Roy Reznik
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2025)
forbes_bio: Roy Reznik cofounded Israeli cloud security business Wiz and owned a 10% stake in the company.
Google's parent company Alphabet acquired Wiz for $32 billion in cash in March 2026.
Wiz software scans storage providers such as Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure to flag and prioritize security risks.
The company's revenue surpassed $100 million in 2023, when the founders began their "suicide plan" of hiring fast, raising funds and targeting top-of-market corporations.
Wiz customers include Fox, Morgan Stanley and LVMH, whose billionaire CEO wrote the unicorn a personal check.

name: Jacky Xu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2019); Forbes annual (2012-2018); Hurun Global (2022-2024)
forbes_bio: Jacky Xu runs and owns most of Trendy International, a popular apparel company with brands that include Ochirly and Five Plus.
L Capital, a private equity group backed by French luxury goods giant LVMH, bought a reported 10% of Trendy in 2011 for $200 million.

name: Tom Werner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Tom Werner rose to prominence as a TV executive, producing hits like That 70's Show and 3rd Rock From The Sun, as well as Roseanne and The Cosby Show prior to their controversies.
In 2001, Werner cofounded Fenway Sports Group (then called New England Sports Ventures) and bought the Boston Red Sox for $380 million a year later.
Werner owns more than 10% of FSG, which controls the Red Sox, Liverpool FC and the Pittsburgh Penguins, and counts LeBron James as an investor.
forbes_facts: Werner's first foray into Major League Baseball was as majority owner of the San Diego Padres in 1990.
Werner first became a Red Sox fan while studying at Harvard in the late 1960s.

name: Emma Marcegaglia
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Emma Marcegaglia is the CEO and chairman of Marcegaglia Holding, which owns Italian steelmaker Marcegaglia, the world's largest maker of welded tubes.
She owns half of Marcegaglia, with the other half owned by her brother Antonio; the siblings took over after the death of their father Steno in 2013.
Steno founded the company in 1959 in the northern Italian city of Mantua and grew it into a multinational firm with operations on multiple continents.
Marcegaglia processes 6.2 million tons of steel a year and posted $6.6 billion in sales in 2019.
From 2008 to 2012, she served as the president of Confindustria, Italy's largest business association and chamber of commerce.
forbes_facts: She was the chair of the board of Italian oil major Eni from 2014 to 2020.
She also served as the president of Luiss Guido Carli University in Rome.
